title: Drift-aware quant fidelity monitoring and dynamic rollback gating
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build an automated eval + alerting pipeline that detects quality regressions caused by quantization profile or model-configuration changes, with the ability to dynamically gate or roll back deployments when fidelity drops beyond a measured budget. This ticket focuses on the monitoring and gating layers (not the quant kernels themselves).

Key ideas and acceptance criteria:
- Fidelity metric: define a composite "fidelity score" that combines embedding cosine similarity, token-level KL divergence, and task-specific pass/fail (e.g., QA F1, summarization ROUGE-L). Score must be normalized to 0-100.
- Drift-awareness: compare incoming post-deploy traffic distribution (prefix lengths, token entropy, prompt categories) to the baseline used during quant-profile selection. Use distribution shift signals to weight the fidelity score conservatively when drift is high.
- Per-profile sensitivity sampling: run lightweight per-layer stochastic perturbation tests (N=50 sequences) for AWQ and GPTQ variants to estimate expected variance; include these in the profile metadata returned by the model catalog.
- Dynamic threshold annealing: thresholds are not static; implement scheduled annealing that tightens gating during canary and relaxes slightly for mature releases according to observed variance.
- Automated gating actions: when fidelity score falls below the computed threshold AND drift-alert is triggered, perform: 1) immediate traffic split to fallback float32/dedicated variant, 2) create an incident ticket with diagnostics, 3) flag the model version in the console for rollback.
- Alerting and dashboard: add per-model and per-profile fidelity heatmaps, time-series of composite scores, and top-10 failing prompts. Wire alerts to PagerDuty with pre-condition that run-rate > X requests/min to avoid noise.
- Evaluation harness: integrate with existing eval-runner but add new checks: logit mean diff, token-level KL, and chain-of-thought consistency checks for reasoning prompts. Ensure end-to-end runs complete within 20m for canary sizes (~5k samples).

Deliverables:
- New fidelity_score computation module + tests.
- Drift detector that emits a drift_score and prompt-category breakdowns.
- Gating service that evaluates fidelity_score + drift_score and runs rollback actions via rollout API.
- Console dashboard panels and alerting rules.
- Runbook describing triage and rollback steps.

Non-goals: full retraining or quantizer fixes (these will be routed to research/quant infra teams), changing existing kernel implementations.

Success metrics:
- False positive gating rate < 1% on canary runs for the next two releases.
- Mean time to detect regression < 10 minutes after deployment when regression > 5 points on fidelity_score.
- Reduction in customer-facing regressions due to quant profile changes by 70% in Q2 post-launch.
updates: 2026-02-22: Initial design review with PM and SRE. Agreed on composite fidelity_score components and drift-weighting idea. PM requested inclusion of per-customer gating option for enterprise customers.
2026-02-26: Prototype fidelity_score implemented in eval-runner. Early experiments show embedding cosine and KL are correlated but provide orthogonal signals on generative variability.

2026-03-03: Integration spike with rollout API finished. Canary traffic split demo successful; fallback to dedicated variant works end-to-end in staging. Added telemetry hooks for per-prompt failing traces.
2026-03-10: UX sync — console team provided mockups for heatmaps and top-failing prompt lists. Decided to show both raw metrics and normalized fidelity_score. Added PagerDuty routing rules draft.
2026-03-12: Added stochastic per-layer sampling for AWQ profiles (N=50) and stored sensitivity metadata in profile registry. Started working on gating thresholds annealing algorithm.
comments: PM comment (Riley Chen, 2026-02-22): Please include a clear per-release signal so sales/CS can be notified when an enterprise customer's pinned model is affected.

Design comment (Lina Gomez, 2026-03-01): For the top-10 failing prompts widget, let's sanitize customer data and show prompt fingerprints instead of raw prompts. UX will provide a tooltip for retrace links.
Eng comment (Somesh Iyer, 2026-03-05): We need rate guards on the drift detector; low-volume customers should not trigger noisy rollbacks. Consider requiring run-rate > 30 req/min in the past 5m.
SRE comment (Jordan Lee, 2026-03-08): Add a rollout safety TTL so automatic rollback doesn't thrash in flapping conditions; use exponential backoff for re-enabling an edged profile.
runbook: Step 1: On alert, confirm fidelity_score and drift_score spikes in Grafana. Step 2: Check top failing prompts and sample traces. Step 3: If confirmed and customer impact > medium, trigger rollback via rollout API and page SRE. Step 4: Attach failing prompt set to ENG quant infra queue with profile metadata. Step 5: Follow up: schedule deep regression eval with research team and owner.
next_steps: (1) Finish threshold annealing algorithm and unit tests. (2) Complete console panels and front-end integration. (3) Run 3 staged canaries in staging and collect false-positive stats. (4) Publish runbook and ship in runtime-1.22.
notes: This ticket intentionally separates detection/gating from mitigation (quant fixes). Close collaboration with research (quant team) required for remediation. Consider later extension to per-customer fidelity budgets and UI controls for 'relaxed mode' on trusted customers.
